Wake the Steward and point to the good player marked with the Know reminder, then put them back to sleep. If the Steward is drunk or poisoned, you may point to any player, even an evil one. While preparing the first night, put the Know reminder by any good character token - the token must already be placed before this step runs.

setup.instructions: Put the Know reminder by any good character token before night 1.

first.instructions: If there is only one Village Idiot in play, they are sober. If there are two or three, exactly one of them is drunk - place the Drunk reminder on them now, and never move it afterwards. Wake each Village Idiot one at a time: they point to any player, and you give a thumbs up if that player is good or a thumbs down if evil, then put them back to sleep. The drunk Village Idiot (or any poisoned one) may be given false information.

other.instructions: Wake each Village Idiot one at a time: they point to any player, and you give a thumbs up if that player is good or a thumbs down if evil, then put them back to sleep. The drunk Village Idiot (marked Drunk) or any poisoned Village Idiot may be given false information. The Drunk marker never moves: if every sober Village Idiot leaves play, or a sober one is made drunk by something else, the marked one stays the drunk one. If a Village Idiot is created mid-game, only one is created.

setup.instructions: [+0 to +2 Village Idiots] - decide how many are in play. If there is more than one, mark exactly one of them Drunk now, and never move that token.

first.instructions: During Minion Info, show each Minion the Damsel character token so they learn a Damsel is in play; they do not learn who it is. If Minion Info was skipped (for example by a Poppy Grower), show them at your first opportunity. The evil team gets ONE guess in total, however many Minions are in play: the first time any Minion publicly guesses a player as the Damsel, mark Guess Used - right or wrong, that is their only guess. If the guess is correct, evil wins. The Damsel is not woken here, unless the Huntsman chose them tonight, in which case show them the YOU ARE info token and their new character token.

other.instructions: Only act if the Huntsman chose the Damsel tonight. If so, wake the Damsel, show the 'You are' info token and a not-in-play Townsfolk character token of your choice, then put them back to sleep and swap their token in the Grimoire. Only the HUNTSMAN's state matters: if the Huntsman is sober and healthy, a drunk or poisoned Damsel still becomes a Townsfolk.

day.instructions: The evil team has ONE guess in total. The first time any Minion publicly guesses a player as the Damsel, mark Guess Used. If the guess is right, evil wins; if it is wrong, they never get another.

The Golem may nominate only ONCE all game. When they do, if the nominee is not the Demon, that player dies immediately. Mark May Not Nominate afterwards. A drunk or poisoned Golem kills nobody but still spends the nomination.

other.instructions: Only act if the Hatter died today or tonight (the Tea Party Tonight reminder). Wake the Minions and the Demon together; each may keep their current character or point to any other character of their own type (Minions choose Minion characters, the Demon chooses a Demon character). If two of them would end up as the same character, shake your head at the LATER chooser and make them pick again - including a player who wanted to stay as they are. For each player who changes, show the THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU info token and the Hatter token, then their new character token, swap their token in the Grimoire, and put everyone back to sleep. Remove the Tea Party Tonight reminder afterwards. If the Hatter was drunk or poisoned when they died, no one may change character.

reference.instructions: Whoever wins, LOSES, and whoever loses, wins - applied as the very last step of the win check. It works while the Heretic is dead, and is suppressed while the Heretic is drunk or poisoned.

setup.instructions: [-0 or -1 Outsider] - decide which before filling the bag, and write it down.

reference.instructions: The Hermit has ALL Outsider abilities on the script at once. Wake them at every in-play Outsider's night step and use those Outsiders' reminder tokens; if the Hermit duplicates an Outsider who is in play, use the Hermit's own 1, 2 and 3 reminders instead.

first.instructions: Wake the Ogre and have them point to a player other than themself, then put them back to sleep. Place the Friend reminder on the chosen player: the Ogre becomes that player's alignment but does not learn which alignment it is, so give no signal. This works even if the Ogre is drunk or poisoned. If the Ogre pointed to an evil player, turn the Ogre's character token upside down - they are now evil. The Friend reminder is an optional rule; under the base rule the Ogre's alignment simply becomes the chosen player's.

other.instructions: Only act if the Plague Doctor has died and you have not yet gained a Minion ability. Choose a Minion character (usually not in play) and gain its ability yourself as Storyteller, placing the Storyteller Ability reminder to track it; if the ability affects setup or ongoing play, apply it as sensibly as possible. Do not tell the players which ability you gained. If the gained ability acts at night, add a night token for it to the night sheet and run it at that character's usual position every night from now on. If the Plague Doctor was drunk or poisoned when they died, you gain no ability.

reference.instructions: If the Politician was the player most responsible for their own team losing, they change alignment and win instead, even if dead. Decide it at the end of the game, not before.

day.instructions: One player is drunk because of the Puzzlemaster - mark them. Once per game the Puzzlemaster may publicly guess who it is: tell them who the Demon is, but if the guess was wrong, name a wrong player instead. Mark Guess Used either way.

first.instructions: Before the Demon receives its bluffs, wake each Minion one at a time, show the 'These characters are not in play' info token and 3 not-in-play character tokens as bluffs, then put them back to sleep. Each Minion may be shown different bluffs. If the Snitch is drunk or poisoned, the Minions do not receive bluffs.

shows.label: Minion bluffs
shows.text: THESE CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY

setup.instructions: Each Minion gets 3 not-in-play character tokens of their own as bluffs - choose them before the first night. With a Marionette in play, the Marionette gets none and the Demon gets an extra 3 instead.

reference.instructions: If 5 or more players are alive, the Zealot MUST vote on every nomination. Remind them at the table rather than penalising them.

first.instructions: Wake the Boffin and the Demon together. Show both the 'This character selected you' info and the Boffin token, then show the not-in-play good character token whose ability the Demon has. Both players now know which good ability the Demon carries. Put both to sleep and run the granted ability at its usual place in the night order for as long as the BOFFIN is alive, sober and healthy: if the Boffin dies or is drunk or poisoned, the Demon temporarily loses the good ability.

setup.instructions: Choose which good ability the Demon will have - a Townsfolk or Outsider ability from this script. The Demon cannot be given the Drunk, Heretic, Ogre or Politician ability.

day.instructions: If the Boomdandy is executed, all but 3 players die IMMEDIATELY. Count down from 10 out loud; on '1' every surviving player points at another player, and the player with the most fingers pointed at them is executed. Run it fast and loudly - the chaos is the point.

first.instructions: Wake the Fearmonger. They point to a player; place the Fear reminder on that player and put the Fearmonger to sleep. At dawn, publicly announce that the Fearmonger has chosen a player (do not say who). If the Fearmonger later nominates and executes the marked player, that player's team loses immediately.

other.instructions: Wake the Fearmonger. They point to a player; move the Fear reminder there and put them to sleep. If the choice is different from last night, announce at dawn that the Fearmonger has chosen a player; if it is the same player, make no announcement. If the Fearmonger nominates and executes the marked player, that player's team loses. If the marked player is executed but does not die, their team still loses.

day.instructions: If the Goblin publicly claims to be the Goblin, mark them with the Claimed reminder. If they are executed while that token is on them, EVIL WINS. The claim must be public, and a drunk or poisoned Goblin's claim does nothing.

first.instructions: Wake the Harpy. They point to one player, THEN another - one at a time, not two at once; mark the 1st with the Mad reminder and the 2nd with the 2nd reminder, then put the Harpy to sleep. Wake the 1st target, show the 'This character selected you' info and the Harpy token, then point clearly at the 2nd target, and put them back to sleep. Tomorrow the 1st player must act mad that the 2nd player is evil, or you may kill one or both of them.

other.instructions: Wake the Harpy. They point to one player, THEN another - one at a time, not two at once (either may be a dead player, in which case only the living one can be killed); move the Mad reminder to the 1st and the 2nd reminder to the 2nd, then put the Harpy to sleep. Wake the 1st target, show the 'This character selected you' info and the Harpy token, then point at the 2nd target, and put them to sleep. The penalty is a DAY-time decision, not a night kill: tomorrow, if the player marked Mad is not mad that the player marked 2nd is evil, you may kill one or both of them during the day.

day.instructions: Watch the player marked Mad. If they are not mad that the player marked 2nd is evil, you may kill one or both of them - during the DAY, not at night.

first.instructions: Do not wake the Marionette - they think they are the good character they drew and get that character's fake info at the appropriate times. They are also never woken for any step that would confirm they are a Minion: Minion Info, Snitch, Preacher, Lil' Monsta, Poppy Grower, Hatter and Damsel all skip them. Wake the Demon, show the 'This player is' info and the Marionette token, then point at the Marionette player. Keep the 'Is The Marionette' reminder on that player. Remember the Marionette must neighbor the Demon and is actually evil, drunk-like: their ability does not work.

setup.instructions: The Marionette must be sitting NEXT TO THE DEMON. Deal the bag as normal, then pick one of the Demon's two good neighbours, take their character token, and give them the Marionette token face down without telling them - they keep believing they are the good character they drew. Place the Is The Marionette reminder on that seat. They are evil and their ability does not work.

first.instructions: Wake the Mezepheles and silently show them their secret word (write it beforehand and show it as text - do not speak). Put them to sleep. Remember the word: the first good player to say it - publicly OR privately, including privately to you - becomes evil that night.

other.instructions: If a good player said the secret word today, wake that player, show the 'You are' info token and give a thumbs-down: they are now evil (same character, evil alignment). Mark them with the Turns Evil reminder resolved and mark the Mezepheles with No Ability - only the first good player ever turns. Turn the turned player's character token upside down in the grimoire and remove the Mezepheles' night token from the night sheet. If the MEZEPHELES is drunk or poisoned on the night a player would turn, the player stays good and the Mezepheles has still used their ability - mark No Ability; they may not turn anyone later. (Optional flavour, not a rule: you may wake the new evil player alongside the Demon so the evil team can learn its new member.)

setup.instructions: Write the secret word down before the game. Pick something a player will plausibly say out loud but not in the first minute.

first.instructions: Wake the Organ Grinder. They nod yes to be drunk until dusk, or shake their head no to stay sober; mark them with the Drunk reminder if they nod. Put them to sleep. Remember that all day, but only while the Organ Grinder is SOBER: votes happen with eyes closed, and you say nothing at all when a vote ends - not the tally, and not whether the nominee is about to die. Mark the current front-runner with the About To Die reminder and only when nominations close do you declare that the marked player is executed. If the Organ Grinder is drunk, the vote happens with eyes open as normal and you make no comment about why.

shows.label: Ask
shows.text: DRUNK TODAY? NOD YES / SHAKE NO

shows.label: Vote result
shows.text: NOMINATIONS ARE CLOSED. THIS PLAYER IS EXECUTED.

other.instructions: Wake the Organ Grinder. They nod yes to be drunk until dusk, or shake their head no to be sober; add or remove the Drunk reminder accordingly. Put them to sleep. During the day, but only while the Organ Grinder is SOBER, run all votes with eyes closed and say nothing when a vote ends - not the tally, not whether the nominee is about to die. Track the front-runner with the About To Die reminder and declare the execution only when nominations close. A drunk Organ Grinder means an ordinary eyes-open vote, with no comment from you. Dead players may still vote once if they hold a vote token; take that token at the END OF THE DAY rather than after the vote, so nobody can count. Players may not use touch or sound to work out who is voting.

shows.label: Ask
shows.text: DRUNK TODAY? NOD YES / SHAKE NO

day.instructions: Each day, BEFORE nominations, the Psychopath may publicly choose a player: that player dies. If the Psychopath is executed, they duel the executioner - both roll or guess a number; if the Psychopath wins, they do not die and the other player does.

first.instructions: There is no Demon in play yet - do not do a normal demon setup. Wake the Summoner, show the 'These characters are not in play' info token, then show 3 not-in-play good character tokens as bluffs. Put them to sleep and place the Night 1 reminder on the Summoner. Nobody dies at night until the Summoner acts on night 3.

shows.label: Bluffs
shows.text: THESE 3 CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY…

other.instructions: Advance the Summoner's night reminder (Night 2, then Night 3). On night 3, wake the Summoner: they point to a player and choose a Demon character (let them pick from the script's demons). Put the Summoner to sleep, wake the target, show the 'You are' info and the chosen Demon token and give a thumbs-down - that player is now that evil Demon and acts tonight if their ability allows. If the Summoner dies before creating the Demon, GOOD WINS IMMEDIATELY - at that moment, not on night 3. If the Summoner is alive but drunk or poisoned on night 3 so that no Demon can be created, good wins as well. This is a rule, not a storyteller judgement. The new Demon does not learn which players are the Minions, and the Minions do not learn the new Demon.

shows.label: Night 3: to target
shows.text: YOU ARE… THIS DEMON, AND EVIL

first.instructions: The Vizier does not wake. When the first night has ended, publicly announce which player is the Vizier. Remember during the day: the Vizier cannot die by execution or other day deaths, and after a vote is tallied, if at least one GOOD player voted on THAT nomination, the Vizier may choose to have the nominee executed immediately. It counts as the day's one execution, and no more nominations, votes or executions happen today.

Wake the Widow and show them the Grimoire for as long as they need (cover any reminders you must hide, e.g. a fellow Widow's Know token). They then choose a player: mark that player with the Poisoned reminder - they stay poisoned as long as the Widow lives. Put the Widow to sleep. Choose a good player, mark them with the Know reminder, wake them and show the Widow token so they learn a Widow is in play.

The Wizard only acts if they are making their once-per-game wish; establish a signal (e.g. they may leave you a note or you wake them to ask). If they wish tonight, hear the wish and decide whether to grant it, what price it carries, and what clue about the wish you will give the good team. Do whatever setup the granted wish requires and use the '?' reminders to track its ongoing effects.

other.instructions: If the Wizard has not yet wished, check whether they wish tonight and, if so, decide whether to grant it, its price, and the clue you will leave for the good team. If a granted wish has ongoing effects, resolve them at whatever point in the night order fits, tracking them with the '?' reminders. If you DECLINE a wish, the ability is not spent: prompt the Wizard to wish again on a later night. When you grant one, signal it clearly ('Your wish is granted') and make the clue about its nature a PUBLIC declaration. Only a granted wish ends the Wizard's ability.

day.instructions: The clue about a granted wish is declared PUBLICLY. A declined wish does not spend the ability.

first.instructions: The Wraith may open their eyes at any point during the night, and wakes whenever any other evil player wakes - Minion Info, Demon Info, and every evil character's own step. Wake them alongside those steps so the evil team is never surprised by an open pair of eyes. They take no action of their own.

other.instructions: Wake the Wraith whenever other evil players wake. They may open their eyes; they take no action.

first.instructions: The Xaan does not wake. You secretly chose X during setup: X is the number of Outsiders in play DURING SETUP, and it never changes, even if the number of Outsiders changes later. If X is 1, mark the Xaan with the X reminder: all Townsfolk are poisoned tonight until dusk - give them false info accordingly. Otherwise place the Night 1 reminder to start counting.

other.instructions: Advance the Xaan's night reminder each night. When the night number equals X, and only if the XAAN IS ALIVE, replace it with the X reminder: every Townsfolk is poisoned from that night until dusk, so their abilities malfunction and their info may be false. The poison ends at dusk the following day; after night X the Xaan has no further effect.

setup.instructions: Secretly choose X = the number of OUTSIDERS IN PLAY DURING SETUP. Write it down. X never changes, however the Outsider count moves later. Place the Night 1 reminder to start the count.

other.instructions: Wake the Al-Hadikhia. They may choose 3 players, in order; mark them with the 1, 2 and 3 reminders and put the demon to sleep (the Al-Hadikhia may choose itself). One at a time and in order, wake each chosen player, announce aloud for all to hear something like 'You are the first/second/third chosen - live or die?'; they silently nod to live or shake their head to die - say NOTHING about their answer - then put them to sleep and wake the next. Resolve each answer as it is given: a player who chooses to live has their shroud REMOVED (this can bring a dead player back to life), a player who chooses to die is given a shroud. When all three have answered, if all three are alive - none has a shroud - then all three die. A player who chose to die but did not actually die counts as alive for that check. All players must be SILENT from the moment you declare that a player has been chosen until you declare that the silence has ended; declare both. At DAWN, declare for each of the players marked 1, 2 and 3 whether they are alive or dead - even if nothing changed for them.

shows.label: Ask each chosen
shows.text: DO YOU CHOOSE TO LIVE OR TO DIE?

first.instructions: There are no pre-set Minions - the Kazali creates them now. Wake the Kazali: they point to each player they want as a Minion and pick which Minion character each becomes, one at a time, until the NORMAL NUMBER OF MINIONS for this player count exists. Only Minions that are on the script may be chosen, and no two may be the same Minion. Put the Kazali to sleep, then wake each chosen player, show the 'You are' info and their new Minion token and give a thumbs-down; they are now that evil Minion. Swap the grimoire tokens accordingly and run any setup those Minions cause (e.g. a Kazali-created Widow or Boffin) as best fits; Outsider counts may have been changed at setup.

shows.label: To each chosen
shows.text: YOU ARE… THIS MINION, AND EVIL

other.instructions: Wake the Kazali. They point to a player; that player dies - mark them with the Dead reminder. Put the Kazali to sleep and announce the death at dawn.

setup.instructions: The bag contains NO Minions - the Kazali creates them on the first night. Fill those slots with Townsfolk or Outsiders, and decide the Outsider count you want the Kazali to be able to reach.

other.instructions: Legion does not wake - you decide the kill. Choose whether a player dies tonight and who (you may kill a Legion player or a good player; killing no one is allowed). Mark the victim with the Dead reminder and announce at dawn. During the day: if a nomination gathers enough votes to put a player on the block but ONLY EVIL PLAYERS VOTED, declare that its tally is ZERO - that is not the same as a failed execution, because a later nominee with fewer votes can still go to the block. Legion registers as a Minion as well as a Demon. Aim to reach three players alive; on the final day, if the town does not execute, kill a good player. If only one good player remains alive, you may declare that evil wins.

setup.instructions: [Most players are Legion] - fill most of the bag with Legion tokens and deal the rest as good characters. Every Legion player is evil and registers as a Minion as well as a Demon.

reference.instructions: Legion has no first-night step of its own: it is handled inside DEMON INFO. During that step, let all Legion players make eye contact with each other, and you may point to the non-Legion players so Legion knows who they are. If a Magician is in play, wake Legion in separate groups instead, and no group learns the Magician.

first.instructions: The Leviathan does not wake and never kills. At dawn, publicly announce that the Leviathan is in play, and place the Day 1 reminder. Track executions of good players with the Good Player Executed reminder: if a second good player is ever executed, evil wins immediately. ALL types of execution count, even when the player does not die - a Virgin execution, a revealed Mutant, a Pacifist save, a Devil's Advocate save all still count as executions.

shows.label: Public announce
shows.text: THE LEVIATHAN IS IN PLAY. IT IS DAY 1.

other.instructions: Advance the Leviathan's day reminder to the coming day; you may publicly re-announce that the Leviathan is in play and which day it is. Nobody dies at night. If more than one good player has been executed, or day 5 ends with the Leviathan alive, evil wins.

shows.label: Public announce
shows.text: THE LEVIATHAN IS IN PLAY. IT IS DAY…

first.instructions: Lil' Monsta is a token, not a player. Skip the Minion Info and Demon Info steps entirely on the first night. Wake all Minions together; the majority silently point until they settle on ONE player to babysit Lil' Monsta tonight - it may be any player, not only a Minion, and a good player who babysits 'is the Demon' while remaining good. Put the Minions to sleep, wake the chosen babysitter, show the 'You are' info and the Lil' Monsta token, and place the 'Is The Demon' reminder on them - they register as the Demon while babysitting. Nobody dies on the first night.

shows.label: To babysitter
shows.text: YOU HOLD LIL' MONSTA - YOU ARE THE DEMON

other.instructions: Wake all Minions together; they silently agree who babysits Lil' Monsta tonight (it may be the same player). Put them to sleep, wake the new babysitter, show the 'You are' info and the Lil' Monsta token, and move the 'Is The Demon' reminder to them. Then a player might die - you choose who (typically as a demon kill); mark them Dead and announce at dawn. If the Minions cannot reach a unanimous decision, YOU decide. The player marked Is The Demon registers as the Demon: if they die, declare that the game is over and good has won.

shows.label: To babysitter
shows.text: YOU HOLD LIL' MONSTA - YOU ARE THE DEMON

first.instructions: Wake the Lleech. They point to a player; mark that player with the Poisoned reminder - this is the Lleech's host, poisoned for as long as the Lleech is alive and has its ability. Put the Lleech to sleep. Remember the Lleech cannot die by any means while the host lives, and dies immediately when the host dies.

other.instructions: Wake the Lleech. They point to a player; that player dies - mark them Dead and announce at dawn (they may kill their own host, which then kills the Lleech too). Put the Lleech to sleep. If anything would kill the Lleech while its host lives, the Lleech does not die - unless the Lleech is drunk or poisoned, in which case the host is not poisoned and the Lleech dies normally. If the Lleech survives an execution, tell the group the player lives, but not why. when the host dies by any means, the Lleech dies immediately.

first.instructions: The evil team sits in a line with the Lord of Typhon in the middle; its neighbors were made Minions at setup. During setup, remove all Minion tokens from the bag and add Townsfolk or Outsider tokens in their place; after the deal, replace the good character tokens of the players sitting outward from the Lord of Typhon with those Minion tokens - as many on each side as this player count needs (3 Minions at 10-12 players, 4 at 13-15), so it is not always two. Wake the appropriate number of players directly clockwise and anti-clockwise, one at a time: show the 'You are' info and their Minion token and give a thumbs-down - they now know they are that evil Minion (they do not automatically learn who the demon is; run minion/demon info per your script). Put each to sleep before waking the next. Do not wake the Lord of Typhon itself. Then run the Minion Info and Demon Info steps as normal.

shows.label: To each neighbor
shows.text: YOU ARE… THIS MINION, AND EVIL

other.instructions: Wake the Lord of Typhon. They point to a player; that player dies - mark them with the Dead reminder. Put the demon to sleep and announce the death at dawn.

Wake the Ojo. They choose a character, not a player, by pointing at a character icon on their own character sheet. If that character is in play, that player dies - and if more than one player is that character, only one of them dies (you choose). If the named character is not in play, you choose any player to die instead, and you should almost always kill a living good player - mark the victim with the Dead reminder. Put the Ojo to sleep and announce the death at dawn.

Riot does not kill at night. Advance the Riot day reminder to the coming day. On night 3, wake all Minion players one at a time, show the YOU ARE info token and the Riot token, and REPLACE their Minion tokens with Riot tokens in the grimoire. The nominee-dies rule applies on DAY 3 ONLY: each nominee dies immediately and must then nominate an alive player straight away - tell them to nominate again and count down '3... 2... 1...' out loud. If the town does not nominate at all, or a nominee runs out of time, nominate a player yourself. The day runs nomination to nomination until all Riot are dead (good wins) or just 2 players are alive (evil wins).

first.instructions: Wake the Yaggababble and silently show them their secret phrase (write it beforehand and show it as text - do not speak). Put them to sleep. During each day, keep a private count of every time the Yaggababble says the phrase publicly.

other.instructions: The Yaggababble does not wake. For each time they said their secret phrase publicly today, a player might die - you choose how many of those potential kills happen and who dies (use the Dead reminders). You may kill at the Yaggababble's place in the night order or at any point afterwards up until dawn. Announce the deaths at dawn. If the Yaggababble is drunk or poisoned at the moment the kill would happen, nobody dies - even if they were sober when they said the phrase - and the converse also holds.

Before dawn, choose a player who is NOT marked Not Me - the Cacklejack named a player during the day, and the target must be a different one. Wake the target, show the YOU ARE info token and their new character token, and swap their token in the grimoire.

day.instructions: Each day the Cacklejack chooses a player and you mark them with the Not Me reminder - that player is the one who will NOT change character tonight; a different player does.
Once per day the Gangster may choose to kill one alive NEIGHBOUR, but only if their other alive neighbour agrees to it out loud. Both neighbours must be alive.

As soon as the Gnome enters play, mark a player of the same alignment as the Gnome with the Amigo reminder and announce publicly which player that is. The Gnome never wakes at night.

During the day, if anyone nominates the Amigo, the Gnome may choose to kill the nominator immediately - but it is the GNOME's responsibility to speak up, and you may not prompt them. They must do it before you start the voting process. The nominator dies at once, and the vote for the nominee still happens.

shows.label: Public announce
shows.text: THIS PLAYER SHARES THE GNOME'S ALIGNMENT...

first.instructions: Announce which players are protected by the Angel - the new players you chose - and mark them with the two Protected reminders.

setup.instructions: Choose the new or inexperienced players the Angel protects and mark them Protected. If something bad happens to a protected player because of another player's actions, that player's team may suffer for it: place the Something Bad reminder and act on it.

reference.instructions: Something bad happening to a protected player is a Storyteller judgement, and it is meant to be visible: say that the Angel is in play at the start of the game.

first.instructions: Announce which players are affected by the Buddhist.

reference.instructions: For the first 2 minutes of each day, the affected players may not talk. Call the start and the end of the silence out loud.
At least once this game you will make a mistake, correct it, and publicly admit it. Place the Whoopsie reminder when it happens so the table can see the promise was kept.

setup.instructions: Read out every jinx on this script BEFORE the game starts, whether or not the jinxed characters were dealt - reading them all is how the good team learns nothing from which ones you read. The app's Jinxes list is the script's jinxes, not the dealt ones. Write down any special rule you add so you can quote it verbatim later.

reference.instructions: The Djinn's special rule is whatever the jinx says. If a jinx changes a night procedure, run the jinxed version, not the character's usual one.

day.instructions: If 4 or more players are alive, each living player may ONCE per game publicly choose a player of their own alignment: that player dies immediately. Announce the death and move on quickly.

other.instructions: Only act if EXACTLY THREE players volunteered to visit the Duchess today. If more or fewer than three volunteered, place no reminders at all and skip the Duchess entirely. Wake each player marked Visitor or False Info one at a time: show them the THIS CHARACTER SELECTED YOU info token and the Duchess token, then a finger signal for the number of evil players among the marked visitors - except for the player marked False Info, who must be shown any number other than the true one. Put each player back to sleep before waking the next, then clear the Visitor and False Info reminders.

shows.label: Show Duchess token
shows.text: This many of the Duchess's visitors are evil (see my fingers)

day.instructions: On the FINAL day, all dead players regain their vote token. Declare the final day explicitly - the app asks you to at 3 players alive - and hand the tokens back before nominations open.

reference.instructions: Once per game you may give ONE good player a piece of incorrect information from any ability. Mark the Fibbin with No Ability afterwards so you remember it is spent.

day.instructions: Once per game, the Demon secretly chooses an opposing player. Then every player publicly chooses which of those two players they want to win, and that side wins the game. Run it as a formal vote with everyone pointing at once.

reference.instructions: If a player talks when the Storyteller has said there must be silence, something bad happens to them - say so at the start of the game, and follow through the first time.

setup.instructions: Pick 2 NEIGHBOURING players who are the same alignment, mark them with the two Aligned reminders, and announce publicly which pair it is. Decide, once, whether one of them registers falsely and mark Register Falsely? if so.

reference.instructions: The pair is known to be the same alignment. Once per game one of them may register as the other alignment - that is the whole of the ability.

setup.instructions: [There might be 1 extra or 1 fewer Outsider in play] - decide before you fill the bag, and do not tell anyone which way you went, or whether you used it at all.

reference.instructions: There cannot be more than 1 extra evil player - place the No More Evil reminder once that limit is reached and refuse any further conversions.

first.instructions: Resolve the Minion Info and Demon Info steps even though there are fewer than 7 players - that is the Toymaker's whole first-night job, and it is easy to miss. Then mark the Demon with the Final Night: No Attack reminder: it records that the Demon still OWES the table one night with no attack, and comes off the first night they decline to attack.

other.instructions: The Demon may choose to make no attack tonight, and must do so at least once per game; if they signal no attack (for example a thumbs-down or crossed arms), nobody dies. If it is a night when a Demon attack could win the game and the Demon is marked Final Night: No Attack, do not wake the Demon at all - they do not act tonight. The Final Night: No Attack reminder means the obligation is still OUTSTANDING, not that it has been spent: place it on the Demon at the start of the game and remove it the first night the Demon declines to attack.

reference.instructions: Each nominee chooses a player: until voting starts, only that player may speak, and they are mad that the nominee is good or they might die. Enforce the silence yourself.

setup.instructions: The Bootlegger carries this game's homebrew rules. Write them down, announce them before the game, and use the two ? reminders for anything that needs tracking.

reference.instructions: Whatever house rules you declared with the Bootlegger apply.

setup.instructions: You assign ALL players' characters instead of dealing a bag. Build the whole grid deliberately - this is the Fabled that gives you total control of the setup.

reference.instructions: One player wears the Ug hat (place the Hat reminder). While wearing it they may only speak one sound at a time, but their vote counts twice. If they fail, the hat passes to another player.
The first 4 players to die are immediately reincarnated as Travellers of the same alignment. Run the normal Traveller arrival for each of them, at the moment they die.
There are two Storytellers: one lies, one tells the truth. Once per game, at dusk, they may switch which is which - silently.

setup.instructions: There are duplicate GOOD characters in play - deal two copies of one or more good characters. Those characters may also appear among the Demon's bluffs.

first.instructions:
Announce which good character is STORMCAUGHT (you chose it before the game, and declared at the start of the game that a Storm Catcher is in play). Two branches, and the app must run whichever applies.

If that character IS in play: mark that player with the Stormcaught reminder. Wake each evil player one at a time, show them the character token, then point at the marked player, and put them back to sleep. While the marked player has their ability they can only be killed by execution - and the Stormcaught token lasts all game, so do not sweep it at dawn.

If that character is NOT in play: point at nobody. Wake each evil player one at a time, show them the THESE CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY info token and the favoured character token, then put them back to sleep.

Source note for the lead: roles.json says the reminder is Stormcaught and the not-in-play branch shows THESE CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY, while the wiki's older How to Run still says a SAFE reminder and a THIS PLAYER IS token. roles.json is the newer source and matches the reclassification to Loric, so it is what this entry follows.

shows.label: Not in play
shows.text: THESE CHARACTERS ARE NOT IN PLAY

first.instructions: Skip the Minion Info and Demon Info steps entirely - nobody knows who they are, so there is nothing to reveal.

other.instructions: If a player died tonight, wake them, show the YOU ARE info token and their character token, and give a thumbs up for good or a thumbs down for evil. They learn who they were only now.

setup.instructions: Nobody learns their character or alignment. Deal the bag as normal but hand out no tokens: keep every character token in the grimoire and tell the table what is happening.

reference.instructions: If a player is mad as a fresh character during their own nomination, you may decide they do not die if executed today. Mark them Mad; it expires at dusk.
One or more players each have a secret goal - mark them with the Goal reminders (there are three). When a player achieves their goal, tell them one piece of true information.
